# A path parameter needs a server, and the static build says so.
#
# It used to be able to ask whether the href was a literal: the checker
# desugared `"/p/{pkg}"` into a concatenation, so anything with a placeholder
# in it was not one. The path is a plain string now and the placeholders are
# ordinary characters, so `/p/{pkg}` is a perfectly good literal -- read for
# that alone the static build wrote a directory named `{pkg}` and said nothing
# at all.

! sngl generate --lang none --platform html -o out app.sngl
stderr 'window "home" has a dynamic href'
! exists out/p

# A path with no placeholders is still a page.
sngl generate --lang none --platform html -o out plain.sngl
exists out/index.html

-- app.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"
import "sngl:platform/html"

struct PageParams {
    pkg string
}

ui.window #home(title="t", href=`/p/{pkg}`, params=PageParams{}) {
    ui.text(value="pkg is {v.pkg}")
}

-- plain.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"
import "sngl:platform/html"

ui.window #home(title="t", href="/index.html") {
    ui.text(value="plain")
}
